CheckTitle: Ensure IAM password policy requires at least one uppercase character
Description: The IAM account password policy should require at least one uppercase letter. Character class requirements are a component of the broader password complexity configuration covered by AWS Security Hub FSBP IAM.11.
Risk: Passwords without required character classes have reduced entropy against dictionary and pattern-based attacks, though the primary driver of password strength is length (CIS 1.8) rather than character class diversity.
Remediation: Update the IAM account password policy to require uppercase characters via the AWS Management Console or CLI: aws iam update-account-password-policy --require-uppercase-characters.
SeverityBasis: AWS Security Hub FSBP IAM.11 (broadly covers strong password policy configuration); NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 IA-5(1)(h) (organization-defined complexity rules). Not a standalone numbered control in CIS AWS 3.0.0; low severity reflects component-level nature of the check.
AuthoritativeSource: AWS Security Hub FSBP IAM.11; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5
CISControl: N/A — character class requirements are not individually enumerated in CIS AWS 3.0.0 (see CIS 1.8 for minimum length and CIS 1.9 for reuse)
